report.source_text: Two weeks prior to this hospital admission, she developed a fever, cough and back pain amidst the COVID-19 pandemic. The patient tested positive for COVID-19 and was treated with azithromycin for 5 days at home. Subsequently, over the next 2 weeks, her fever and cough resolved, but the lower back pain persisted. This was characterised by a throbbing, 7/10 intensity (numeric rating scale), radiating to both the lower extremities. She then had a new onset of numbness, pins and needles sensation in the left lower extremity associated with mild weakness. These same symptoms then progressed to the contralateral lower extremity over the next 24 hours with an unstable gait. This progression triggered an emergency room visit. She had no headaches, loss of consciousness, changes in mental status, changes in vision and speech, difficulty swallowing, seizure-like symptoms or urine/bowel incontinence.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 58-year-old woman developed fever, cough, and back pain and tested positive for COVID-19. After resolution of fever and cough, she experienced persistent back pain followed by progressive lower extremity numbness, pins and needles sensation, mild weakness, and unstable gait. Initial physical exam showed stable vitals, 5/5 motor strength, and normal deep tendon reflexes with unremarkable conus medullaris on MRI lumbar spine. Routine labs revealed mild leukocytosis; imaging excluded acute brain or spinal lesions but showed degenerative spine changes. Within 24 hours, neurological worsening occurred with muscle strength declining to 3/5 bilaterally in lower extremities and new left upper extremity weakness, accompanied by diminished deep tendon reflexes. Lumbar puncture was performed to rule out GBS but CSF results are not documented in the provided data.

Progressive ascending weakness and sensory symptoms following COVID-19 infection
Development of diminished deep tendon reflexes and clinical worsening consistent with Guillain-Barré syndrome
Routine labs and imaging excluding other acute intracranial or spinal causes
